from_quote: as the Constitution has established the trial by jury in criminal cases
rationale: In stating the objectors' argument, the paragraph names the Constitution's establishment of "the trial by jury in criminal cases," the subject of this clause.

from_quote: This discretion, in regard to criminal causes, is abridged by the express injunction of trial by jury in all such cases
rationale: Names "the express injunction of trial by jury" in all criminal causes, echoing this clause's words "The Trial of all Crimes ... shall be by Jury."
to_quote: The Trial of all Crimes, except in Cases of Impeachment, shall be by Jury

from_quote: All land causes, except where claims under the grants of different States come into question, and all other controversies between the citizens of the same State
rationale: In saying which causes the national judiciary will not hear, the paragraph excepts claims to land "under the grants of different States" between citizens of the same State, echoing this clause's words.
to_quote: between Citizens of the same State claiming Lands under Grants of different States

from_quote: The trial by jury in criminal cases, aided by the habeas-corpus act, seems therefore to be alone concerned in the question. And both of these are provided for, in the most ample manner, in the plan of the convention.
rationale: Names "the trial by jury in criminal cases" as "provided for ... in the plan of the convention," the subject of this clause.

from_quote: aided by the habeas-corpus act, seems therefore to be alone concerned in the question. And both of these are provided for, in the most ample manner, in the plan of the convention
rationale: Says habeas corpus is, with criminal jury trial, "provided for ... in the plan of the convention"; this is the only clause of the plan that names habeas corpus. The paragraph's own words are "the habeas-corpus act," not the wording of the clause.
to_quote: The Privilege of the Writ of Habeas Corpus

from_quote: the appellate jurisdiction in matters of fact being vested in the Supreme Court
rationale: The footnote names "the appellate jurisdiction in matters of fact being vested in the Supreme Court," pointing to No. 81, where this clause's words "appellate jurisdiction, both as to law and fact" are quoted.
to_quote: appellate Jurisdiction, both as to Law and Fact
